abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are regulators of metabolism, yet how physiological GC exposure remodels adipose metabolism and its relationship with circulating biomarkers remains poorly understood. In a randomised cross-over study of individuals with primary adrenal insufficiency, near-physiological GC exposure was compared to withdrawal using integrated serum metabolomics, abdominal subcutaneous microdialysis metabolomics, and adipose tissue transcriptomics. GC exposure induced coordinated changes in adipose lipid and amino-acid metabolism. Pathway-level entropy analysis revealed GC-state-dependent transcriptional reorganisation, with concentrated organisation during exposure and diffuse organisation during withdrawal. Integrative hypergraph and topological analyses revealed GC-state-dependent reorganisation of circulating metabolite-adipose tissue relationships, with greater higher-order coordination during exposure. The circulating phenylalanine/kynurenine ratio discriminated GC state, showed the strongest shared connectivity to GC-regulated adipose networks, persisted at midnight and in an independent dose-response study, and exhibited circadian rhythmicity. These findings reveal dynamic GC regulation of adipose metabolism and identify a circulating biomarker with potential to guide personalised GC therapy.
